_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when prioritizing work in an AI-assisted codebase, designing agent autonomy levels, deciding what to automate vs…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "we keep adding tooling and the agent throughput isn't going up — what TOC step are we missing?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the constraint-awareness skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is constraint-awareness the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes constraint-awareness as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against ai-native-development, agent-engineering, code-review
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the constraint-awareness workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore constraint-awareness
Does not route to ai-native-development, agent-engineering, code-review when the constraint-awareness scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "what's the ICE / RICE score for this initiative against five others"
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should constraint-awareness be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside constraint-awareness's ownership
Routes the work to ai-native-development or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying constraint-awareness terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply constraint-awareness as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if constraint-awareness has a secondary support role

Does not use constraint-awareness's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
